main_body: Beehive-shaped thatched hut: a tall conical straw roof dominating the upper part, over a short clay/mud wall with a dark arched doorway
top_band: Thatch roof slope, light straw tones with banded courses, rows ~4-56 down the centre column; the roof is seen from above and flares out into an eave with a dark underside at rows ~56-58
evidence: The thatch cone is a large sloped surface that is clearly visible from above, with horizontal courses and a lighter crown. It overhangs the wall and casts a dark shadow band at rows ~56-60 on the clay wall below. The wall (rows ~58-78) is a separate vertical face with its own shading and a stone base. The doorway is inset, with a dark frame and an inner shadow, and it cuts into the roof as an arch. Both the roof surface and the front face are clearly drawn, so it reads as 3/4 and not as an elevation.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 straw tones, dark brown course lines, and per-bundle dashes that give a strong rhythm. The outline is dark brown, a tinted version of the neighbouring material, not black. The clay wall has about 4 steps with brick-like dashes and a speckled stone base, which makes it a little simpler than the roof. The door interior is a flat dark fill but is small. Overall this sits acceptably next to the reference house roofs, though the wall is a bit less rich than the reference walls.
